changes: Use ownedProjectedScanInputs and the shared bounded deferred gather for borrowed and owned projected limit queries.
Remove the accumulated row-reference implementation and unused row-key/batching helpers; offset skipping no longer retains a query-wide reference list.
Enable owned projected results for borrowed vector scanners, preserving detached mutable values and explicit result lifetime.
Retain the early input independently through asynchronous late reads and enforce cancellation before output projection.

coverage: Offset 9 versus 999 at fixed batch size has the same observed allocation peak; exact peak succeeds and one byte less rejects.
Borrowed binary payload remains unchanged after scanner reuse; owned outputs retain charges until release.
Late read failure/cancellation closes early and late iterators and releases reservations.
Real Parquet HTTP matrix covers borrowed/owned, ranked/unranked, valid 206/ignored Range, 64/128 MiB pools and four concurrent cold/warm jobs.
Deferred 206 output transfers less than half the eager bytes; ignored-range fallback transfers no more than eager; warm jobs need no data ranges beyond discovery probes.

compatibility: Unordered deferred limits no longer charge a serialized row-reference list because that state was removed. Allocation budgets still bound batch/gather/output work; ordered top-k retains its serialized-state boundary tests.
remaining: Projected read-column planning helpers still need complete admission integration.
Borrowed scanner internal decode/metadata allocations and runtime overhead are not made globally bounded by detaching returned batches.
Broader audit and whole-runtime cloud memory acceptance remain open.
